From weapon motion
to material response.

The study follows one impact through detection, evaluation and presentation. Reusable weapon and material presets keep the calculations separate from the authored response.

Technical systems.

01 / Motion & collision

Track the contact region

During the attack window, a SphereCast sweeps between successive positions of the weapon’s detection point. Each collider registers once per swing.

Sweep radius sets the width of the contact test. The solver divides effective force by contact area to calculate pressure.

02 / Impact solver

Evaluate before presenting

Weapon mass and sampled velocity determine the strength input. The solver checks alignment and relative hardness before classifying the hit by pressure.

A head-on strike aligns with the inward surface normal. A glancing strike travels across the surface.

03 / Shader Graph

Localize and release the deformation

Material hardness and elasticity scale the displacement. Spatial falloff localizes it, while hold time, damped oscillation and reduced rebound control its recovery.

A MaterialPropertyBlock supplies each renderer with its own hit parameters. Contact area sets the visual radius.

04 / Data & presentation

Share the evaluated impact

ScriptableObjects hold weapon and material presets. A common ImpactData event feeds VFX and Debug observers; deformation is called directly on the receiver.

Each material selects its particle prefab. Effects face the surface normal, with a small downward spawn offset.

Comparing responses.

Hammer on three materials.

Metal
Brief sparks Stretched spark streaks mark contact with the hard-surface target.
Slime
Indentation + droplets A local depression recovers as blue droplets leave the surface.
Stone
Brittle debris Mesh particles tumble away from the point of contact.

Three weapons on Slime.

Spear, hammer and sword strike Slime with different motion and weapon settings. The localized response follows each recorded contact.

Iterations & evidence.

Contact area ≠ collision radius

Splitting the two controls corrected early contact on broad weapons without changing the pressure model.

Geometry is part of the shader

Slime’s topology and normals were revised to address faceting and uneven highlights during development.

A clearer third material

Carapace became Metal so the target and spark effect expressed the same material idea.

Runtime debugging

The hammer strike on Slime registers a pressure of 8.08 and a solver deformation force of 6.46. The Debug Panel reads the same event as the VFX manager. ImpactReceiver scales the solver force by the material properties before passing it to the shader.

Architecture and Shader Graph captures

Scope & sources.

A single swept point represents the weapon’s contact region. The shader displaces rendered vertices while mesh topology and collision geometry stay fixed.

Each renderer stores its most recent hit. Each impact spawns a separate material-specific particle effect.
